executive_summary.login_failure_root_cause: The frontend makes /auth/me a hard prerequisite for both rendering /login and entering protected routes, but neither the browser fetch nor the Next proxy fetch has a timeout. If /api/backend/auth/me or the backend fetch never settles, PublicOnly/AuthGuard remain in checking/loading state indefinitely. After login, AuthProvider.login also waits for a second /auth/me before redirect completion. In addition, current /auth/me returns only basic identity and no permissions, while the frontend still treats user.permissions as the owner/full-access source, causing authenticated users to lose owner UI capabilities.
executive_summary.dashboard_white_screen_root_cause: The dashboard is hard-blocked first by AuthGuard while AuthProvider is checking /auth/me. After authentication, dashboard content is not a pure white-screen crash, but it can remain loading because OperationsDashboard waits for Promise.allSettled over refreshCapabilityState plus four dashboard APIs, and refreshCapabilityState itself is a 9-request capability fan-out with no timeout. One hung request keeps dashboard loading active forever.
executive_summary.provider_architecture_root_cause: Provider state is split across CapabilityStateProvider, AdapterAccessProvider, and ModuleAccessProvider, which independently request overlapping module, adapter, and execution-provider state. Sidebar and route guard can read different copies of the same backend facts. AuthProvider still owns permissions even though /auth/me no longer returns them.
executive_summary.api_fan_out_root_cause: Initial dashboard load duplicates capability requests: CapabilityStateProvider fires 9 requests, AdapterAccessProvider repeats 4 of them, ModuleAccessProvider repeats /modules/me, and OperationsDashboard immediately calls capabilityState.refresh(), repeating the 9-request fan-out again.
executive_summary.missing_product_functionality_root_cause: Most non-user-management product pages are read-only list shells or explicit empty states. Adapter/execution-provider metadata is fetched, but the action layer is not mounted or executable. /permissions/me exists and is allowlisted but is not bound to AuthProvider.

flow: RootLayout wraps all pages in AuthProvider.
AuthProvider useEffect calls refresh() on mount.
refresh() sets status=checking and awaits currentUserRequest().
apiRequest() fetches /api/backend/auth/me with credentials=include and no timeout.
Next proxy maps auth/me to backend /api/public/auth/me.
PublicOnly blocks /login while status is checking.
login() awaits POST /auth/login, then awaits GET /auth/me again.
LoginForm redirects with router.replace('/dashboard') only after login() resolves.
